claim: A 96-well plate assay allows fast, reproducible, and high-throughput generation of 3D cardiac rings around a deformable optically transparent hydrogel (polyethylene glycol [PEG]) pillar of known stiffness.
source: We developed a 96-well plate assay which allows fast, reproducible, and high-throughput generation of 3D cardiac rings around a deformable optically transparent hydrogel (polyethylene glycol [PEG]) pillar of known stiffness.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of the developed assay.

claim: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes mixed with normal human adult dermal fibroblasts in an optimized 3:1 ratio self-organized to form ring-shaped cardiac constructs.
source: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, mixed with normal human adult dermal fibroblasts in an optimized 3:1 ratio, self-organized to form ring-shaped cardiac constructs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Fibroblasts form a basal layer in contact with the glass, stabilizing the muscular fiber above.
source: Immunostaining showed that the fibroblasts form a basal layer in contact with the glass, stabilizing the muscular fiber above.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Tissues started contracting around the pillar at D1.
source: Tissues started contracting around the pillar at D1 and their fractional shortening increased until D7, reaching a plateau at 25±1%, that was maintained up to 14 days.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by video evidence (Figure 1—video 1) and data in Figure 3.

claim: The fractional shortening of tissues increased until D7, reaching a plateau at 25±1%, that was maintained up to 14 days.
source: Tissues started contracting around the pillar at D1 and their fractional shortening increased until D7, reaching a plateau at 25±1%, that was maintained up to 14 days.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The average stress calculated from the compaction of the central pillar during contractions was 1.4±0.4 mN/mm2.
source: The average stress, calculated from the compaction of the central pillar during contractions, was 1.4±0.4 mN/mm2.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The cardiac constructs recapitulated expected inotropic responses to calcium and various drugs (isoproterenol, verapamil).
source: The cardiac constructs recapitulated expected inotropic responses to calcium and various drugs (isoproterenol, verapamil) as well as the arrhythmogenic effects of dofetilide.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: The cardiac constructs recapitulated the arrhythmogenic effects of dofetilide.
source: The cardiac constructs recapitulated expected inotropic responses to calcium and various drugs (isoproterenol, verapamil) as well as the arrhythmogenic effects of dofetilide.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D-E.

claim: The heart lacks regenerative capacities.
source: As the heart lacks regenerative capacities, CTE emerged in the field of regenerative medicine with the objective of producing cardiac grafts that can be implanted in patients with heart failure (Madonna et al., 2019; Jabbour et al., 2021; Eschenhagen et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Cardiac tissue engineering emerged in the field of regenerative medicine with the objective of producing cardiac grafts that can be implanted in patients with heart failure.
source: As the heart lacks regenerative capacities, CTE emerged in the field of regenerative medicine with the objective of producing cardiac grafts that can be implanted in patients with heart failure (Madonna et al., 2019; Jabbour et al., 2021; Eschenhagen et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Engineered heart tissues have provided essential platforms for cardiac disease modeling.
source: While these EHTs recapitulate a limited number of functions in vitro, they have provided essential platforms for cardiac disease modeling (Filippo Buono et al., 2020; Cashman et al., 2016; Williams et al., 2021; Stillitano et al., 2016; Bliley et al., 2021; Goldfracht et al., 2019; Richards et al., 2020) and drug development (Beauchamp et al., 2015; Polonchuk et al., 2017; Zhao et al., 2019; Mannhardt et al., 2020), reducing the need for animal studies.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations to the literature.

claim: Engineered heart tissues have provided essential platforms for drug development, reducing the need for animal studies.
source: While these EHTs recapitulate a limited number of functions in vitro, they have provided essential platforms for cardiac disease modeling (Filippo Buono et al., 2020; Cashman et al., 2016; Williams et al., 2021; Stillitano et al., 2016; Bliley et al., 2021; Goldfracht et al., 2019; Richards et al., 2020) and drug development (Beauchamp et al., 2015; Polonchuk et al., 2017; Zhao et al., 2019; Mannhardt et al., 2020), reducing the need for animal studies.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations to the literature.

claim: Different combinations of cells, biomaterials, and scaffolds have successfully generated 3D EHTs with various geometries including spheroids, cardiac strips, circular bundles, myocardium-like sheets, or ventricle-like chambers.
source: Different combinations of cells, biomaterials, and scaffolds have successfully generated 3D EHTs (Seguret et al., 2021; Zhuang et al., 2022) with various geometries including spheroids (Beauchamp et al., 2015; Polonchuk et al., 2017; Giacomelli et al., 2020; Richards et al., 2020; Hofbauer et al., 2021; Lewis-Israeli et al., 2021), cardiac strips (Hansen et al., 2010; Legant et al., 2009; Turnbull et al., 2014; Mannhardt et al., 2016; Nunes et al., 2013; Zhao et al., 2019), circular bundles (Goldfracht et al., 2020; Tiburcy et al., 2017; Li et al., 2020), myocardium-like sheets (Shadrin et al., 2017), or ventricle-like chambers (MacQueen et al., 2018; Li et al., 2018; Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations to the literature.

claim: EHTs are optimally formed by mixing hiPSCs-derived cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, and/or other cell types such as endothelial cells to more closely mimic the structure and cellular complexity of native myocardium.
source: The EHTs are optimally formed by mixing human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs)-derived cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, and/or other cell types such as endothelial cells to more closely mimic the structure and cellular complexity of native myocardium (Giacomelli et al., 2020; Saini et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to the literature.

claim: A major obstacle in the development of EHTs is the inevitable trade-off between the need for miniaturization to increase throughput and the biological complexity of the tissues.
source: However, a major obstacle in the development of EHTs is the inevitable trade-off between the need for miniaturization to increase throughput (i.e. several organoids in each well of a 96- or 384-well plate) and the biological complexity of the tissues (Cho et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The mold fits in the well of a 96-well plate and consists of 21 identical conical structures with a central hole.
source: The mold fits in the well of a 96-well plate and consists of 21 identical conical structures with a central hole (Figure 1A, left).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1A showing the mold design.

claim: The interior profile of the cavity was shaped in a reversed hourglass.
source: These showed that the interior profile of the cavity was shaped in a reversed hourglass, as expected.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1B showing PDMS replica images.

claim: The Young's modulus of 5% PEG gels is 11.4±0.5 kPa.
source: The values obtained (11.4±0.5 kPa) are within the physiological range for human cardiac tissue (Gershlak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The Young's modulus of 5% PEG gels is within the physiological range for human cardiac tissue.
source: The values obtained (11.4±0.5 kPa) are within the physiological range for human cardiac tissue (Gershlak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The efficiency of the differentiation of iPSCs into cardiomyocytes was in average of 96.9±0.8%.
source: The efficiency of the differentiation of iPSCs into cardiomyocytes was in average of 96.9±0.8% (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Initial tests with cardiomyocytes resulted in cell cluster formation and malformation of the rings.
source: Initial tests with cardiomyocytes resulted in cell cluster formation and malformation of the rings (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A showing brightfield images.

claim: The 3:1 hiPSC-CMs:fibroblasts ratio was determined to be optimal as it allowed the generation of the highest number of tissues stable in time.
source: The 3:1 hiPSC-CMs:fibroblasts ratio was determined to be optimal as it allowed the generation of the highest number of tissues stable in time, and we could not see any difference in the contractile parameters of the tissues with different fibroblast ratios (see Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Tissues started beating within 24 hours after seeding.
source: Tissues started beating within 24 hours after seeding (Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by video evidence.

claim: An average of 10.75±0.48 tissues per well were obtained which were stable over time for at least 20 days with the 3:1 hiPSC-CMs:fibroblasts ratio.
source: In these optimization experiments, we obtained an average of 10.75±0.48 tissues per well which were stable over time for at least 20 days with the 3:1 hiPSC-CMs:fibroblasts ratio.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The fibroblasts are concentrated at the base of the ring in contact with the glass.
source: The fibroblasts are concentrated at the base of the ring in contact with the glass (Figure 2C – bottom panel), whereas the cardiomyocytes form a compact ring above the fibroblasts around the central pillar (Figure 2C – top panel).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The cardiomyocytes form a compact ring above the fibroblasts around the central pillar.
source: The fibroblasts are concentrated at the base of the ring in contact with the glass (Figure 2C – bottom panel), whereas the cardiomyocytes form a compact ring above the fibroblasts around the central pillar (Figure 2C – top panel).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Troponin T staining evidenced the formation of striated elongated fibers, which are typical of cardiac tissue.
source: Troponin T staining evidenced the formation of striated elongated fibers (Figure 2D), which are typical of cardiac tissue.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The obtained cardiac tissues are 75.5±1.8 µm high and their shape is toric.
source: The obtained cardiac tissues are 75.5±1.8 µm high and their shape is toric, as shown in the 3D reconstruction (Figure 2E and Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by 3D reconstruction data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: One day after seeding the fibroblasts are not yet attached, although the cardiac fiber has already started to be formed.
source: It appears that 1 day after seeding the fibroblasts are not yet attached, although the cardiac fiber has already started to be formed.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Seven days after seeding, fibroblasts are fully spread and attached, and the contractile ring is formed and well aligned.
source: Seven days after seeding, fibroblasts are fully spread and attached, and the contractile ring is formed and well aligned.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Tissues started contracting less than 24 hr after seeding, which was visible through the deformation of their central pillar.
source: Tissues started contracting less than 24 hr after seeding, which was visible through the deformation of their central pillar (Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by video evidence.

claim: The beat rate of the tissues first decreased between day 1 and day 3 and increased again to reach 0.58±0.030 Hz on day 14.
source: The beat rate of the tissues first decreased between day 1 and day 3 and increased again to reach 0.58±0.030 Hz on day 14 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The contraction stress developed by the tissues increased from day 1 until day 7.
source: The contraction stress developed by the tissues increased from day 1 until day 7 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: At day 7, the contractility parameters stabilized with an average stress of 1.4±0.1 mN/mm2.
source: At day 7, the contractility parameters stabilized with an average stress of 1.4±0.1 mN/mm2 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The relaxation and contraction speeds increased during the first 7 days, then reaching a plateau.
source: Consistently, the relaxation and contraction speeds also increased during the first 7 days, then reaching a plateau (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: The tissue depolarization induced a visible increase in fluorescence.
source: We found that, as expected, the tissue depolarization induced a visible increase in fluorescence (see Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: All the pixels were synchronous and no sparks or re-entrant waves could be detected.
source: All the pixels were synchronous and we could not detect any sparks or re-entrant waves (see Figure 4—video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by video evidence.

claim: The repolarization signal is noisy, as it occurs during the time when the tissue deformation is greatest and is probably affected by tissue motion.
source: We also observed that the repolarization signal is noisy, as it occurs during the time when the tissue deformation is greatest and is probably affected by tissue motion.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and represents an observation with a speculative explanation.

claim: The changes in the contraction stress and the contraction and relaxation speeds with calcium concentration were significant (p<0.0001 for each parameter).
source: The changes in the contraction stress and the contraction and relaxation speeds with calcium concentration were significant (p<0.0001 for each parameter, non-significant for the beat rate).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: A positive inotropic response was observed as the contraction amplitude increased by 600% with a corresponding EC50 of 1.346 mM with a CI of [1.159;1.535] mM.
source: We observed a stabilization of the beat rate around 0.5 Hz at 2 mM and a positive inotropic response as the contraction amplitude increased by 600% with a corresponding EC50 of 1.346 mM with a CI of [1.159;1.535] mM.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The changes in the beating parameters with verapamil concentration were found to be significant (p=0.0053 for the beat rate and p<0.0001 for the other parameters).
source: The changes in the beating parameters with verapamil concentration were found to be significant (p=0.0053 for the beat rate and p<0.0001 for the other parameters).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The addition of verapamil, an L-type calcium channel inhibitor, induced a negative inotropic effect until the complete stop of contraction at 10 µM.
source: The addition of verapamil, an L-type calcium channel inhibitor, induced a negative inotropic effect until the complete stop of contraction at 10 µM, as expected (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The IC50 for verapamil was estimated to be 0.677 µM, CI=[4.278;12.81]·10-7 M.
source: The IC50 was estimated to be 0.677 µM, CI=[4.278;12.81]·10-7 M.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: A trend toward increase of the contraction amplitude was observed with isoproterenol, as well as a significant increase in the contraction and relaxation speeds, without change in the beat rate.
source: We observed a trend toward increase of the contraction amplitude, as well as a significant increase in the contraction and relaxation speeds (Figure 5C), without change in the beat rate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The changes in the contraction stress and the contraction and relaxation speeds with isoproterenol concentration are significant (p=0.0004 for the contraction stress; p<0.0001 for the contraction and relaxation speeds).
source: The changes in the contraction stress and the contraction and relaxation speeds with isoproterenol concentration are significant (p=0.0004 for the contraction stress; p<0.0001 for the contraction and relaxation speeds).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Dofetilide significantly reduced the contraction stress and speeds until the complete stop of the contraction of the cardiac tissues for a concentration of 10 nM.
source: As shown in Figure 5D, dofetilide significantly reduced the contraction stress and speeds until the complete stop of the contraction of the cardiac tissues for a concentration of 10 nM.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The changes in the beat rate, the contraction stress, and the contraction and relaxation speeds with dofetilide concentration were found to be significant (p<0.0001 for all the parameters).
source: The changes in the beat rate, the contraction stress, and the contraction and relaxation speeds with dofetilide concentration were found to be significant (p<0.0001 for all the parameters).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Arrhythmic events were noted after adding dofetilide at concentrations of 3 nM and 7 nM.
source: Arrhythmic events were noted after adding dofetilide at concentrations of 3 nM and 7 nM.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The Poincaré diagram for the different dofetilide concentrations shows an increase in the contraction-to-contraction intervals for some cells at 1 nM of dofetilide and an increasing number of erratic beats with increasing dofetilide concentrations.
source: Indeed, the Poincaré diagram for the different dofetilide concentrations (Figure 5E) shows an increase in the contraction-to-contraction intervals (equivalent to RR intervals) for some cells at 1 nM of dofetilide and an increasing number of erratic beats with increasing dofetilide concentrations.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: This novel strategy enables the fast and reproducible formation of an important number of cardiac tissues (up to 21 per well in a 96-well format) with a limited number of hiPSC-CMs (112,500 per well).
source: Our main findings are as follows: (1) This novel strategy enables the fast and reproducible formation of an important number of cardiac tissues (up to 21 per well in a 96-well format) with a limited number of hiPSC-CMs (112,500 per well).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a main finding.

claim: In this assay, fibroblasts are essential to generate and maintain the tissue structure, with a 3:1 hiPSC-CMs:fibroblast ratio providing with the best yield of tissue generation.
source: (2) In this assay, fibroblasts are essential to generate and maintain the tissue structure, with a 3:1 hiPSC-CMs:fibroblast ratio providing with the best yield of tissue generation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a main finding.

claim: The self-organized ring-shaped cardiac tissues contract and deform the optically transparent central pillar, which can be recorded and analyzed to estimate the contractile force developed by the tissue.
source: (3) The self-organized ring-shaped cardiac tissues contract and deform the optically transparent central pillar, which can be recorded and analyzed to estimate the contractile force developed by the tissue.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a main finding.

claim: These ring-shaped tissues are compatible with live fluorescence imaging and allow the simultaneous measurement of contractile parameters and another readout provided by a fluorescent probe.
source: (4) These ring-shaped tissues are compatible with live fluorescence imaging and allow the simultaneous measurement of contractile parameters and another readout provided by a fluorescent probe.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a main finding.

claim: These EHTs display concordant responses to positive or negative inotropes, and to arrhythmogenic drugs, as required for drug testing applications.
source: (5) These EHTs display concordant responses to positive or negative inotropes, and to arrhythmogenic drugs, as required for drug testing applications.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a main finding.

claim: The tissues develop a fractional shortening (or contraction strain) of about 25%, which is close to the contraction of a human heart.
source: Our results showed that the tissues develop a fractional shortening (or contraction strain) of about 25%, which is close to the contraction of a human heart (Cheng et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data and a citation to the literature.

claim: The corresponding stress was 1.4 mN/mm2 which is in a similar range to other previously reported tissue-engineered cardiac muscle models with hiPSC-CMs in the literature.
source: The corresponding stress was 1.4 mN/mm2 which is in a similar range to other previously reported tissue-engineered cardiac muscle models with hiPSC-CMs in the literature (Seguret et al., 2021; Turnbull et al., 2014; Shadrin et al., 2017; Zhao et al., 2019; Ronaldson-Bouchard et al., 2018; Goldfracht et al., 2020; Li et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The force generated by the adult human heart muscle is around 44 mM/mm2 for a tissue strip.
source: The force generated by the adult human heart muscle, around 44 mM/mm2 for a tissue strip (Hasenfuss et al., 1991), however remains significantly higher than the force developed by the currently available platforms.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The force generated by the adult human heart muscle remains significantly higher than the force developed by the currently available platforms.
source: The force generated by the adult human heart muscle, around 44 mM/mm2 for a tissue strip (Hasenfuss et al., 1991), however remains significantly higher than the force developed by the currently available platforms.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Fibroblasts have been shown to play a prominent role in the heart as they are crucial in the constitution of the supporting extracellular matrix and contribute to cardiomyocyte electrical coupling, conduction system insulation, vascular maintenance, and stress-sensing.
source: Fibroblasts have been shown to play a prominent role in the heart as they are crucial in the constitution of the supporting extracellular matrix and contribute to cardiomyocyte electrical coupling, conduction system insulation, vascular maintenance, and stress-sensing (Ivey and Tallquist, 2016; Baudino et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Other studies have highlighted the importance of a multi-cellular approach to generate EHTs.
source: Other studies have highlighted the importance of a multi-cellular approach to generate EHTs (Giacomelli et al., 2020; Saini et al., 2015; Amano et al., 2016; Caspi et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The conduction velocity in iPSC-CMs is around 10–20 cm/s, compared to 40–60 cm/s in adult cardiomyocytes.
source: Indeed, it has been shown that the conduction velocity in iPSC-CMs is around 10–20 cm/s, compared to 40–60 cm/s in adult cardiomyocytes (Ahmed et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The EC50 for calcium response is in agreement with the values reported in the literature for EHTs made of hiPSC-CM, which are between 0.4 mM and 1.8 mM.
source: We observed that our tissues presented a positive inotropic response to increasing extracellular calcium concentration with a corresponding EC50 which is in agreement with the values reported in the literature for EHTs made of hiPSC-CM, which are between 0.4 mM and 1.8 mM for the EC50 (Feric and Radisic, 2016; Schaaf et al., 2011; Streckfuss-Bömeke et al., 2013; Mannhardt et al., 2016; Turnbull et al., 2014; Goldfracht et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The IC50 value for verapamil is in the range of reported values in other EHTs: Turnbull et al., 2014, found IC50=0.61 µM and other papers range from 0.3 µM to 0.6 µM.
source: The negative inotropic response to increasing concentrations of verapamil of our constructs was also described in the literature and our IC50 value is also in the range of reported values in other EHTs: Turnbull et al., 2014, found IC50=0.61 µM and other papers range from 0.3 µM to 0.6 µM (Mannhardt et al., 2016; Thavandiran, 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Dofetilide has been shown to induce atrial fibrillation, Torsade-de-Pointes, and heart failure in patients.
source: Other papers have also underlined the pro-arrhythmic effect of dofetilide on iPSCs-CMs (Goldfracht et al., 2019; Patel et al., 2019; Altrocchi et al., 2020; Blinova et al., 2017) and this drug has been shown to induce atrial fibrillation, Torsade-de-Pointes, and heart failure in patients (Abraham et al., 2015; Shantsila et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The SKiPSC-31.3 hiPSC cell line is from a healthy control subject.
source: The SKiPSC-31.3 hiPSC cell line, from a healthy control subject, has been used here and was previously reported (Galende et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section and supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Glucose starvation has been shown to increase dramatically the percentage of cardiomyocytes obtained.
source: These two rounds of glucose starvation have been shown to increase dramatically the percentage of cardiomyocytes obtained (Sharma et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section and supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The circular geometry of these self-organized cardiac tissues induces a homogeneous distribution of the cardiomyocytes and consequently of the contraction forces around the pillar and in the tissue.
source: We found that the circular geometry of these self-organized cardiac tissues induces a homogeneous distribution of the cardiomyocytes and consequently of the contraction forces around the pillar and in the tissue.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and represents an interpretation of the experimental observations.

claim: The presence of the central pillar not only allows resistance to be felt by the tissue, but the control of its stiffness facilitates the calculation of the force developed by the tissue.
source: Importantly, the presence of the central pillar not only allows resistance to be felt by the tissue, but the control of its stiffness facilitates the calculation of the force developed by the tissue.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and represents an interpretation of the design features.

claim: The stiffness of the central pillar can easily be adapted to model a pathological increase or decrease of the extracellular matrix stiffness.
source: Finally, the stiffness of the central pillar can easily be adapted to model a pathological increase or decrease of the extracellular matrix stiffness.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and represents a potential application of the platform.

claim: The fibroblasts additionally play a role in providing a basement support under the cardiomyocytes, in contact with the glass support of the EHTs.
source: In our system, the fibroblasts additionally play a role in providing a basement support under the cardiomyocytes, in contact with the glass support of the EHTs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by immunofluorescence imaging data.

claim: Immunofluorescence imaging showed an organization of the cardiomyocytes parallel to each other, perpendicular to the direction of contraction, with an increased alignment of sarcomeres.
source: Immunofluorescence imaging showed an organization of the cardiomyocytes parallel to each other, perpendicular to the direction of contraction, with an increased alignment of sarcomeres.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The EHTs mimic the composition and organization of the native myocardial tissue, even if only composed of cardiomyocytes and fibroblasts.
source: Our EHTs mimic the composition and organization of the native myocardial tissue, even if only composed of cardiomyocytes and fibroblasts.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and represents an interpretation of the experimental observations.

claim: The constructs showed a spontaneous beating in the day following seeding and this activity was maintained over several weeks.
source: The constructs showed a spontaneous beating in the day following seeding and this activity was maintained over several weeks thus allowing contractile measurements and pharmacological testing in the conditions of auto-pacing.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data.

claim: The required camera speed to detect the conduction in tissues should be at least of 120 fps if we consider a conduction speed of 15 cm/s.
source: However, our constructs are smaller, with a perimeter of about 1.13 mm, and therefore, the required camera speed to detect the conduction in tissues should be at least of 120 fps if we consider a conduction speed of 15 cm/s.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and represents a calculation based on the tissue dimensions and known conduction velocities.

claim: The increase in contraction and relaxation speeds induced by isoproterenol is translated, on average in this study, into an increase in contractile force rather than in an increase in contraction frequency.
source: Our hypothesis is that this increase in contraction and relaxation speeds induced by isoproterenol is translated, on average in our study, into an increase in contractile force rather than in an increase in contraction frequency.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and represents a hypothesis to explain the observed data.

claim: Since hiPSC-CMs are immature cardiac cells, it is rare to obtain a positive force-frequency relationship without any maturation medium or mechanical or electrical training.
source: Indeed, since hiPSC-CMs are immature cardiac cells, it is rare to obtain a positive force-frequency relationship without any maturation medium or mechanical or electrical training.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and represents knowledge about hiPSC-CMs.

claim: The size of the rings is very small compared to native tissue (400 µm).
source: First, the size of the rings is very small compared to native tissue (400 µm).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a limitation of the platform.

claim: All measurements were performed under spontaneous pacing as a specific technique should be developed to allow external pacing of the tissues in the 96-well format.
source: Second, all measurements were performed under spontaneous pacing as a specific technique should be developed to allow external pacing of the tissues in the 96-well format.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a limitation of the platform.

claim: Pharmacological responses, including the detection of the pro-arrhythmogenic effects of dofetilide, were correctly measured under spontaneous beating conditions.
source: Nevertheless, our main results show that pharmacological responses, including the detection of the pro-arrhythmogenic effects of dofetilide, were correctly measured under spontaneous beating conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The miniaturized format of the platform creates some limitations and challenges regarding some experiments, including tissue stretching.
source: Third, the miniaturized format of our platform creates some limitations and challenges regarding some experiments, including tissue stretching.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a limitation of the platform.

claim: The length-tension relationships (Franck-Starling mechanism) were not determined in the tissues.
source: Therefore, the length-tension relationships (Franck-Starling mechanism) were not determined in our tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a limitation of the platform.
